answer: Shared schedulers fail at delayed-reveal booths they cannot precompute. An applicant bonds 11.40 POA and reserves one 9-minute booth at a published graph vertex. The committee writes a 15-byte whisper behind a delayed-write mirror that stays sealed for 80 seconds, then opens a 6-second reply window. The applicant must pull that whisper and return a 21-byte signed digest before the window shuts; peers compare it to the now-unsealed log. Cost: 11.40 POA and one unbatchable booth. A guessed phrase, late digest, or double booking at that vertex burns 61% and darkens the booth for five epochs.
